title: Corey Haines's PR playbook: earning media coverage as a multiplier for distribution
summary: An open-source AI agent skill by Corey Haines on earned media for software products. It frames PR as a multiplier for distribution, not a conversion channel. It covers the four PR modes, story angles, a pitch quality bar, press page setup, crisis response, and what to measure.

principles.text: PR is a multiplier for distribution, not a substitute; earned media won't drive direct conversions.
principles.quote: PR is not a substitute for distribution. It's a multiplier for it.

principles.text: Pitch journalists like customers: specific, useful, fast. The story is the trend, data, conflict or human, with your product as evidence.
principles.quote: The story is not your product. The story is the trend, the data, the conflict, or the human. Your product is the evidence.

principles.text: Chase press for compounding value (authority, relationships, AI-citation surface), not the short-lived traffic bump.
principles.quote: The bump fades in a day; authority, journalist relationships, and AI-citation surface compound.

principles.text: On reactive PR, speed beats polish: a decent pitch in the first hour beats a perfect one on day three.
principles.quote: A B+ pitch in the first hour of a story beats an A+ pitch on day three.

principles.text: Run at least three of four PR modes (reactive, proactive, inbound, owned) rather than over-indexing on one.
principles.quote: Four modes. Most teams over-index on one. Run at least three.

principles.text: Gate every pitch with a quality bar: right beat, clear news hook, complete story in the email, specific subject line, under 150 words, clear ask.
principles.quote: Could this journalist write a complete story from this email alone? (Data, quotes, customer name, contact.)
